role: Topic Analyst — Compute, infrastructure and supply

topic.title: Compute, infrastructure and supply
topic.one_liner: Only $217.9B of $592.1B in deals is firm on T1/T2 sources; 13.0 of 15.8 GW are 'up to'; about 80% of the $518B plan is non-cancelable.

key_metrics.label: Deal-level commitments, desk tally by bucket
key_metrics.value: $592.1B: $217.9B firm (T1/T2), $89.6B cancellable or conditional, $46.8B reported-unconfirmed, $237.8B prospectus second-hand. The prospectus total is at least $518B (T2 total, T3 split).

key_metrics.label: Gigawatts by basis
key_metrics.value: 15.8 GW announced: 13.0 GW are 'up to' ceilings, 2.8 GW contracted or reported site capacity. Three T1 statements put about 2.3 GW online by end-2026 (desk sum, may overlap held capacity).

key_metrics.label: Non-cancelable share of the prospectus plan
key_metrics.value: About 80% of at least $518B, roughly $414B. The Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Broadcom lines sum to $413.7B (79.8%). SpaceX, up to $84.5B, is largely cancelable on 90 days' notice. Non-cancelable hosting was $54.6B at end-2025 (T3, earlier vantage).

key_metrics.label: Compute and infrastructure spend FY2025 and ratio to revenue
key_metrics.value: $7.33B on $4.59B revenue, $1.60 per $1, 58% of operating expenses (T2). WSJ via PYMNTS (T3): $0.71 in Q1 2026 and $0.56 projected for Q2, scope unstated.

key_metrics.label: Largest single counterparty
key_metrics.value: Broadcom-related leases, $161.2B, 31% of the $518.2B named lines (T3). Google plus Broadcom lines are $272.3B, 52.5%. Amazon and Google also carried 47% of FY2025 sales, $2.16B (T3).

key_metrics.label: TPU lessor SPV notes closed
key_metrics.value: $34.5B (A1 $6.0B, A2 $24.0B, B $4.5B; Apollo headlines $35B) for over 1 GW of TPUs on five-year leases. The desk maps it inside the $161.2B lease line, about 21% (inference). A second ~$36B is pitched and unsettled (T3).

what.t: Compute desk tally, Sep 30 (desk arithmetic): $592.1B over 17 deal rows and 15.8 GW, of which 13.0 GW are 'up to' ceilings. Firm on T1/T2 evidence, $217.9B: Amazon, Microsoft, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Akamai, the SPV notes (Riot and RUM tenants are press-named). Cancellable or conditional, $89.6B: SpaceX, Nscale. Reported, unconfirmed, $46.8B: Lambda, Volta, Akamai plan 1. Prospectus coverage only, $237.8B: Google, Broadcom leases net of the SPV.

Reuters, Sep 28 to 29, on a leaked draft prospectus (T2 total, T3 split): at least $518B over about ten years with six partners, roughly 80% non-cancelable or payable regardless of use. Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, Microsoft $31.4B, Broadcom-related leases $161.2B, SpaceX up to $84.5B, AMD over $20B. Amazon and Google routed 47% of FY2025 sales (T3). Anthropic is shifting toward dedicated data centers and leased chips.

Vendor capital and compute owed (prospectus, T3). Amazon: $18.0B invested, $15.0B facility left (10-Q, Jul 31, T1), owed $110B. Google: up to $40B, $30B on targets (TechCrunch, Apr 24, T2), owed $111.1B. Microsoft up to $5B and Nvidia up to $10B (T1 caps), $30B Azure commitment (T1). AMD: up to $5B (T1), tied to deployment milestones (Reuters, T2), owed over $20B. Memory makers joined Series H (T1).

Financing, Jun 2 to Sep 3. Apollo and Blackstone closed $34.5B of SPV notes (A1 $6.0B, A2 $24.0B, B $4.5B) to buy Google TPUs leased to Anthropic for five years, over 1 GW, funded in about 16 stages, with Broadcom residual-value support (Quartz, T2). Blackstone pitched a second ~$36B (Bloomberg, Aug 5, T3). A $15B pre-IPO revolver, against $2.5B in 2025, is nearing final (Bloomberg, Sep 3, T2).

SpaceX, May 6 to Jul 9. Anthropic rents Colossus 1 (live since May, over 300 MW); the $1.25B monthly fee covers Colossus and Colossus II and is terminable by either side on 90 days' notice (SEC, T1). Musk says the firm period is 180 days (TechCrunch, T2). Prospectus coverage: up to $84.5B against $45B nominal (T3). SpaceX competes through Grok and is buying Cursor for $60B (8-K, T1).

Reuters, Sep 28 (T2): FY2025 compute and infrastructure spend was $7.33B, 58% of $12.65B operating expenses, on $4.59B revenue, $1.60 per $1. WSJ via PYMNTS, May 20 (T3): $0.71 in Q1 2026, $0.56 projected for Q2, scope unstated; Q2 revenue came in at $11.5B (Bloomberg, T3). FT, Sep 13 (T3): Q2 adjusted operating income positive; gross margin above 80% before partner share and training.

means.t: The three totals measure different things. The desk's $592.1B adds deal rows of mixed tiers. The Information's $517B is the maximum value of contracts signed since October 2025. The prospectus $518B is ten-year spend with six named partners. Bridge: $592.1B, less $144.8B of deals outside the six, plus $70.9B more on SpaceX, Amazon, Microsoft and AMD in the prospectus, is $518.2B. The 0.2% match with $517B is coincidence.

Fixed costs meet uncommitted revenue, with the same counterparties on both sides. Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Broadcom lines, described as must-pay or largely non-cancelable, sum to $413.7B, 79.8% of $518.2B. Amazon and Google hold 42.7% of the lines and routed 47% of FY2025 sales, while most large clients have no long-term contracts (T3). SpaceX, the flexible line, is cancelable by either side on 90 days' notice.

Capital follows delivery, and others carry the assets. Amazon's facility opens as AWS delivers (10-Q, T1), AMD's equity and Google's $30B gate on milestones or targets, and Nscale's order needs its financing. A lessor issues the TPU notes with Broadcom residual support and Theseus (Macquarie, GIC) funds data centers, so unrated Anthropic pays leases. No filing traces equity cash to a supplier invoice, so the loop is inferred.

The ratio fall reads as fixed-cost absorption, not proven cheaper tokens: Q1 growth ran 80x annualized against a 10x plan (Amodei, T3), so pre-bought capacity carried more revenue. List prices per token fell 73% on Opus and 33% on Sonnet, so at constant mix a revenue dollar needs more compute unless unit cost falls faster. No unit-cost series exists; 2025 cloud inference ran 23% over plan (T3).

implications.t: Reprice by bucket and basis. Firm T1/T2 is $217.9B; the prospectus non-cancelable core is $413.7B; never add them, The Information's $517B or the FT's ~$200B web. Treat 13.0 of 15.8 GW as options; three T1 statements put about 2.3 GW online by end-2026. Campus figures (Rainier 2.2 GW, Monarch 1.37 GW IT, SpaceX fleet 1.4 GW) are not Anthropic's share. Exclude talks and the $50B Fluidstack overlap.

Treat compute as step-fixed. Straight-line over ten years (no schedule exists), $518.2B is $51.8B a year, 80 cents per dollar of the $65B run-rate; the $413.7B core is 64 cents. Amodei says forecasting misses on compute bought years ahead are ruinous (T2). Do not extrapolate the 56-cent Q2 projection: Anthropic warned profit may not last the year, SpaceX's discount has likely lapsed and list prices have fallen.

Underwrite clusters, not logos. By chip class the desk tally is TPU 46%, NVIDIA GPUs 30%, Trainium 17%, other 7%; AMD is unpriced. Four chip families hedge chip risk, yet TPUs run through Google and Broadcom and Nvidia sits under six priced counterparties. Custom silicon is hiring only (T2). Nscale shows $2.6B active TCV against $103.4B contracted and a $1.02B H1 loss. Score delivery risk, not only credit.

Keep capital efficiency on equity only and show lease-financed capacity beside it. Equity raised is $124.254B. PitchBook's $126.754B includes the $2.5B revolver, and its Jul 16 total of $161.254B over-counted by the $34.5B of lessor notes. The $161.2B lease line and the $15B revolver never enter an equity denominator, so equity-only ratios flatter capacity that lessors finance.

second_order: Supplier backlogs lean on one customer. Nscale's $103.4B active-and-contracted TCV is 43% Anthropic by arithmetic, yet only $2.6B is active. The Information puts Anthropic above 40% of Google's disclosed backlog (T3, DISPUTED), and Broadcom's 8-K ties Anthropic's consumption to its commercial success. A thin S-1 commitment table could re-rate these suppliers before Anthropic. Google, Apollo, Blackstone and Nscale's IPO buyers must react.

Duration mismatch. Shell leases run 20 years (TeraWulf, Riot), GPU services six years (Nscale, Volta, RUM) and chip leases five years (SPV), so one shell spans four chip-lease cycles. Obsolescence and refinancing risk sit with Anthropic or its guarantors. Consensus counts gigawatts and dollars, not years.

The IPO is one leg of a larger financing stack. WSJ (T3) has up to $100B at about $2T, The Information (T4) at least $130B, while $34.5B of SPV notes closed in June, about $36B more is pitched and a $15B revolver is nearly final. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs appear as IPO leads, revolver leads and SPV note placers (T2 to T3). Ask the S-1 to show the fees and relationships.

The supply gap runs to 2027 and 2028, and power sets its pace. The draft prospectus expects demand to exceed supply (Reuters, T2). Shells energize from late 2027 (landlord dates; no slippage base rate in the record), so rented scarcity (about $8 to $12 per GPU-hour, desk-derived) and rate limits bridge it. Anthropic pledged to fund grid upgrades and ordered 470 MW of onsite generation from ERock (T1).

Milestone gating correlates failure. Amazon's facility, AMD's equity, Google's $30B and Nscale's financing all open on delivery or targets, so a delivery slip delays capital and capacity together, while a demand slip hits the non-cancelable core and the suppliers' equity marks at once: Amazon carries its stake at $190.4B against $18.0B invested. The usual critique is that circularity inflates demand. It also couples failures.

watch.item: Public S-1 flip: contractual-obligations table, related-party and debt notes, cost of revenue
watch.threshold: Named lines sum to $518.2B, or Nscale, Lambda, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Volta and Akamai ($144.8B at desk values) sit on top. If additive and only the four T1 contracts count as firm, the total nears $663B and the non-cancelable share nears 70% (desk scenario). Also the SpaceX line, Broadcom tranche status, revolver size and draws, and a year-by-year schedule.

watch.item: Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft Q3 filings: facility availability and draws, Anthropic carrying values, commitment notes
watch.threshold: Any draw on Amazon's remaining $15.0B, or availability rising with AWS delivery, shows milestones being hit. A carrying value above $190.4B shows another mark. Alphabet funded dollars against the $10B first tranche, and any guarantee exposure against the FT's up to about $44B.

watch.item: Colossus: 180-day mark and SpaceX Q3 10-Q (Customer B revenue, Colossus II, any 90-day notice)
watch.threshold: 180 days from the May 3 agreement ends about Oct 30 (desk arithmetic). If Customer B is Anthropic (inference), revenue near $3.75B, a full quarter at $1.25B a month, means the contract runs at list; near or below Q2's $1.52B estimate means a cut. Any notice, or tighter Claude Code limits, is the signal.

watch.item: Anthropic Q3 results: compute per revenue dollar on a stated definition, second adjusted operating profit, GAAP cost of revenue
watch.threshold: Reference class: three reported steps, all down ($1.60, $0.71, $0.56), with no peer series and no stable definition. A ratio above 0.56 on the same definition confirms the H2 ramp the company warned about. What is different now: the discount lapse, the price cuts and scarce rented capacity.

watch.item: Broadcom fiscal Q4 results: Anthropic orders, XPV funding stages, second SPV package
watch.threshold: A second package closing at or above the ~$36B pitched, or A2 pricing wider than 5.75%, reads lessor appetite. Funding should reach about $24B by summer 2027 across roughly 16 stages.

watch.item: Nscale IPO and its Qualifying Financing for Monarch
watch.threshold: IPO pricing that funds the campus, disclosure of the Longstop Date and of Anthropic's share of the $103.4B TCV. A failed financing would move $44.6B out of the conditional bucket.

watch.item: Year-end capacity statements: nearly 1 GW of Trainium2/3 (Amazon), over 1 GW of TPUs (Google), CoreWeave online later in 2026, Vera Rubin shipments (late 2026, T3), Azure's Nov 2026 start (prospectus coverage, T3)
watch.threshold: Statements matching the 2026 claims, about 2.3 GW with Colossus 1. Silence, restated dates or late Vera Rubin shipments signal slippage. No slippage base rate is in the record.

watch.item: First energization: Hut 8 Beacon Point (Q1 2027, tenant unconfirmed) and AMD's first 1 GW (1H 2027)
watch.threshold: A slip of a quarter or more at either, or Anthropic confirming the Beacon Point, Riot and RUM tenant, which Bloomberg, The Information and the WSJ name but filings do not.

topic.house_view: (a) Extends: fundamentals differ on axes a multiple ignores, since margin exists on three bases (about 40%, about 44%, above 80%) with no GAAP figure, and about 80% of the $518B plan is non-cancelable. (b) Does not support the 39.75% size from this slice: marketplace fees were about 7.6% of FY2025 revenue (T3), and every compute ratio here is on Anthropic's gross revenue. (c) Extends: $34.5B of closed SPV notes, about $36B pitched and a $15B revolver sit beside a reported $100B IPO raise (WSJ, T3; The Information says at least $130B, T4), so compute financing competes for the same capital in the same window. (d) Confirms: equity raised is $124.254B, PitchBook moved $34.5B of lessor notes out of its total, and the $161.2B lease line sits outside any equity-only denominator. (e) Confirms: one stack mixes about $2.4M per MW-year shells, $12.5M to $16.2M per MW-year GPU services and $7.8 to $11.8 per GPU-hour (desk-derived), so no single sector convention applies.

uncertainties.note: The six named lines sum to the $518.2B headline to the dollar, so Nscale, Lambda, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Volta and Akamai ($144.8B at desk values) are not inside it on this record. AMD, announced Jul 22, is inside and TeraWulf, disclosed Jul 6, is not, so 'the draft predates them' cannot be the whole explanation. Google is at least $111.1B over seven to 10 years plus $161.2B of Broadcom-related leases in prospectus coverage, against about $200B over five years per The Information (T3, DISPUTED); scope and window differ. The split is one Reuters chain (T3). No year-by-year schedule or as-of date exists.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The public S-1 contractual-obligations table and subsequent-events note.

uncertainties.note: Tenant identity and firmness. Riot, RUM, Lambda and Volta tie to Anthropic only through Bloomberg, The Information or the WSJ, and Hut 8 and Lambda do not name Anthropic. Nscale's $44.6B is a maximum, its 460 MW, term and start are press-only, and its order needs Qualifying Financing. SpaceX is about $40B, $45B nominal or up to $84.5B by source, with a 90 to 180 day firm period. Akamai plan 1's Anthropic link is inferred. Event-level fields double count: Broadcom's 3.5 GW sits in two T1 events, and three SpaceX events hold 45,000, 40,000 and 15,000 for one contract, so use the desk table rows.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Anthropic's subsequent-events note, Nscale's unredacted exhibit and the SpaceX 424B4 text.

uncertainties.note: Ratio scope. The record marks the Reuters financials DISPUTED only because two desks tagged different revenue periods, FY2025 $4.59B and Q2 2026 $11.5B; the $7.33B is not contested. PYMNTS, relaying the WSJ, does not say what 'compute' covers in the 71-cent and 56-cent ratios, while $1.60 covers training, inference and other infrastructure. If all-in, H1 2026 compute is about $9.5B, 1.3x FY2025; if a serving subset, training sits on top. OpenAI's FY2025 cost of revenue, 57 cents per net revenue dollar (T3), is the nearest serving reference class. Gross margin appears as about 40% (paying-user costs), about 44% (PitchBook) and above 80% (company-adjusted); no GAAP figure exists.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: S-1 cost of revenue, the training versus inference split and the definition of compute and infrastructure spend.

uncertainties.note: Circularity and the largest line. Both legs sit in T1 documents only for Amazon, whose April headline of $25B is DISPUTED in the record against $5B invested that day; the 10-Q shows $10B funded in Q2 and $15.0B left. Funded amounts for Google's $10B, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD are absent, and no prepayment amount or schedule appears anywhere in the record. Broadcom's 8-K (T1) says consumption depends on Anthropic's continued commercial success while prospectus coverage calls the $161.2B lease line largely non-cancelable, so part of it may bind only as tranches execute. Mapping the SPV notes into that line is the desk's inference. The 10-Q also cites 'contractual obligations related to the performance of AWS chips', content undisclosed.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD filings, and the S-1 lease note with tranche status.

uncertainties.note: Next four quarters. Reference class: landlord and vendor delivery dates. The record holds no slippage base rate for them, so none is assumed. Dated claims: Amazon nearly 1 GW and Google over 1 GW in 2026, AMD 1 GW in 1H 2027, shells from late 2027. What is different: Nscale and the SPV stages depend on financings not yet funded, and Q1 growth ran 80x annualized against a 10x plan, so demand forecasts have missed by a wide margin.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: Landlord and vendor 8-Ks and 10-Qs reporting energization, and year-end capacity statements.

log.text: Read analyst_common.md in full. Slice: category compute plus compute fields elsewhere; tables compute, compute_totals, compute_costs, pricing, capital_summary, prospectus_facts. Slug compute.
q.py --cat compute 2021-01-01 to 2026-09-30: 76 events, every headline read, more than 80 opened in full with notes
q.py --table compute (24 rows, 17 in totals), compute_totals, compute_costs (16 rows), pricing (29 rows), capital_summary, prospectus_facts (76 rows)
q.py --cat debt --full: 16 events on Amazon notes, the $2.5B and $15B revolvers, TPU SPV notes and the PitchBook removal
Scan of all 691 events for compute fields or compute terms outside category compute: 171 headlines reviewed
q.py --conflicts filtered to compute terms: 44 of 158 rows; q.py --open filtered: 58 of 237 rows
q.py --q on rate limit, usage limit, capacity, weekly limit, demand surge, prepay, backstop, guarantee, shortfall, residual value
Reuters leak of the draft prospectus: at least $518B, six partners, about 80% non-cancelable; the six lines sum to $518.2B
Same Reuters review: 47% of FY2025 sales via Amazon and Google ($2.16B), about 16 cents kept, two 12% customers, $54.6B non-cancelable at end-2025
FY2025 compute and infrastructure spend $7.33B, 58% of $12.65B operating expenses, $1.60 per $1 of revenue

KSL copy of the Reuters piece (WebFetch): 80% wording; Google and Amazon 'regardless of usage'; Microsoft non-cancelable except breach; Broadcom largely non-cancelable; xAI largely cancelable on 90 days; AMD cancelability not stated; no mention of TeraWulf, Riot, Nscale, Lambda, Akamai, RUM or Volta
Four non-cancelable lines (Google 111.1, Amazon 110.0, Microsoft 31.4, Broadcom 161.2) sum to 413.7 = 79.8% of 518.2; SpaceX 84.5 plus AMD 20.0 is 104.5; this reproduces the 80% headline

Regrouped compute table rows: firm = AWS 100 + Microsoft 30 + TeraWulf 19 + Riot 9.1 + RUM 13.7 + Akamai 11.6 + SPV 34.5 = 217.9; conditional = SpaceX 45 + Nscale 44.6 = 89.6; reported-unconfirmed = Lambda 35 + Volta 10 + Akamai plan 1 1.8 = 46.8; prospectus-only = Google 111.1 + (Broadcom 161.2 - SPV 34.5) = 237.8; all match compute_totals to the dollar
Bridge to the prospectus: 592.1 - 144.8 (Nscale, Lambda, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Volta, Akamai x2) = 447.3; prospectus adds Amazon +10.0, Microsoft +1.4, SpaceX +39.5, AMD +20.0 = 518.2
Chip-class regrouping of the same rows: TPU 272.3 (46.0%), NVIDIA GPUs 178.3 (30.1%), Trainium 100.0 (16.9%), shells 28.1 (4.7%), CPU 13.4 (2.3%), AMD unpriced; sums to 592.1

If AMD's $20B were also non-cancelable the share would be 83.7% ((413.7 + 20.0) / 518.2); Reuters' 'about 80%' therefore implies AMD sits outside the non-cancelable set or is partly conditional; its terms are not stated

Timing anomaly: the draft includes AMD (announced Jul 22) but omits TeraWulf (disclosed Jul 6), Volta, Riot, Nscale, Lambda, RUM and Akamai, so the desk's 'draft predates the deals' explanation cannot cover TeraWulf; the alternative, leases not yet commenced carried elsewhere, is unverified

Broadcom 8-K (WebFetch): 'The consumption of such expanded AI compute capacity by Anthropic is dependent on Anthropic's continued commercial success'; about 3.5 GW from 2027; no cancellation terms stated

Broadcom 8-K (T1) makes consumption conditional on Anthropic's commercial success while prospectus coverage (T3) calls the $161.2B Broadcom-related lease line largely non-cancelable; the largest line may bind only as tranches execute
Amazon Q2 10-Q: $18.0B invested, $15.0B of a $20.0B facility left, stake carried at $190.4B

Amazon 10-Q (WebFetch): 'At inception, there is no amount available to be drawn against'; amounts become available as delivery milestones of compute capacity are reached; draws are convertible notes, or common stock after an IPO subject to the ownership cap; expires 30 months after a liquidity event
10-Q wording matches the record's draw_mechanics field and the $5.0B Series H purchase that cut the facility to $15.0B
Amazon's April headline is DISPUTED in the record as $25B ($5B now plus up to $20B) versus $5B invested that day; both hold on different bases, and the 10-Q shows $10B funded in Q2 with $15.0B left
Google: up to $40B with $30B on targets (TechCrunch, single T2) and The Information's ~$200B over five years for Google Cloud and chips (T3, DISPUTED)

Google commitment is about $200B over five years (The Information, T3) versus $111.1B plus $161.2B over seven to 10 years (prospectus coverage, T3); scope and window differ; both values named, none picked

Desk compute row gives Google a ~10-year window; Reuters' wording is 'the next seven to 10 years' and the event term field runs Apr 2026 to Jul 2033, about 7 years, so Google's annual payments are higher than a ten-year straight line implies
Microsoft and Nvidia: $30B Azure commitment and up to 1 GW (T1); investment caps $5B and $10B; funded amounts undisclosed
AMD: up to 2 GW from 1H 2027 and up to $5B equity, milestone-based (T1); a T3 report says AMD plans up to $5B of senior notes to fund it
AMD's $5B is equity into Anthropic, not compute spend; press recaps call it a '$5B deal'; the compute value (over $20B) appears only in prospectus coverage
TPU SPV: $34.5B closed (A1 $6.0B, A2 $24.0B, B $4.5B), Broadcom residual support, Anthropic lessee and unrated, about 16 stages; price talk was $35.5B; a second ~$36B is pitched

Broadcom 10-Q commitments note, R17 (WebFetch): a financial partner took over agreements to purchase AI racks; maximum backstop liability about $29B undiscounted on deployment of all racks; the note names no customer and does not mention Anthropic
Broadcom's own $29B maximum backstop matches the record's ~$29B exposure (T3); T1 on the amount, but nothing in the note ties it to Anthropic, so the tie stays an inference
Mapping the $34.5B SPV notes into the $161.2B Broadcom-related lease line is the desk's inference; Reuters does not describe the lessor structure, and verify-operating records the same caveat

Lead outside the record, not used in the analysis: the same Broadcom note also describes a customer option to issue Broadcom convertible notes up to $42B; the customer is unnamed, so any link to Anthropic is unproven
Theseus Infrastructure: Macquarie and GIC fund most project equity for data centers with Anthropic as anchor tenant (Business Wire, T1); no dollars or GW disclosed
Revolvers: $2.5B five-year facility (May 2025); $10B+ target (Aug 18) to $15B with 17 banks (Sep 3); whether it replaces or adds to the $2.5B is undisclosed ($15B or $17.5B)

SpaceX cluster: $1.25B a month and 90 days' notice (SEC letters quoting the S-1); Musk says 180 days; Google pays $920M a month from October; 10-Q Customer B at 19.5% of Q2 revenue; Musk says he will not cut Anthropic off

SpaceX value by source: about $40B (TechCrunch, Musk), $45B nominal (36 x $1.25B), up to $84.5B (prospectus, +88%); event-level compute.usd_m holds 45,000, 40,000 and 15,000 (annual) for one contract, so summing event fields triple counts

Deals outside the six-partner list: TeraWulf, Volta, Riot, Nscale, Lambda, RUM and Akamai (Jul to Sep; plan 1 in May), plus Zerra; WSJ counted about $175B of recent cloud deals (T3, composition not stated)

Tenant identity: Riot (Bloomberg, T2), RUM (The Information, T3), Lambda at Hut 8 (WSJ, T3) and Volta (Bloomberg) name Anthropic only through press; Hut 8 and Lambda do not name Anthropic; the desk keeps Riot and RUM in the firm bucket on T1 amounts

Nscale S-1 (WebFetch): about $2.6B active and $103.4B active-and-contracted TCV at Aug 31; about 461,000 contracted and 25,000 active GPUs; H1 revenue $140.6M, net loss $1,020.1M; Anthropic agreements 'up to approximately $44.6 billion'

Nscale: S-1 text gives only 'up to approximately $44.6 billion'; 460 MW, six years and late 2027 are press-only; the order is conditional on Qualifying Financing; $2.6B active TCV against $103.4B contracted
Akamai: amounts are T1 but the Anthropic link for plan 1 ($1.8B) is inferred; the 8-K covers plans 2 and 3; the ~$20B expansion is TechCrunch-only
Akamai warrant wording is consistent across sources: 40% of the warrant vesting on first payment (8-K) is 2% of Akamai common (release), and each further 20% is about 1%

GW bases differ: IT versus gross power (Nscale 1.37 vs 2.0, Zerra 1.44 vs 2.16, TeraWulf 401 vs 480 MW); two T1 events carry Broadcom's 3.5 GW and the Series H event carries 10.0 GW as a sum of two programs; summing event-level GW double counts

Capacity timing: Rainier about 500K Trainium2 live Oct 2025; Google over 1 GW in 2026; Amazon nearly 1 GW by end-2026; AMD 1 GW in 1H 2027; TeraWulf, Riot, Nscale late 2027 to 2028; Beacon Point first energization Q1 2027
Margins kept apart: 2025 about 40% (paying-user costs; inference cost 23% over plan), PitchBook about 44%, FT above 80% adjusted; WSJ Q2 operating profit includes training and excludes SBC

PYMNTS relay of the WSJ (WebFetch): '71 cents on compute for every dollar of revenue ... 56 cents'; what compute covers is not specified; operating profit includes model training and excludes stock-based compensation; Anthropic cautioned it may not sustain profitability for the full year

Ratio scope: 0.71 and 0.56 have no stated scope; $1.60 is training plus inference plus other infrastructure; desk notes disagree (PitchBook event reads a serving subset, WSJ event note treats it as all-in)

Price table: Opus $15/$75 to $5/$25 (Nov 2025) to $4/$20 (Sep 2026) = -73%; Sonnet $3/$15 to $2/$10 = -33%; Haiku up 4x; cache reads 10% to 2.5% of input; fast mode premium 6x to 2x; Opus 4.7 tokenizer up to +35% tokens
